C_answer_size_is_a_separate_axis.can_fail_because: the answer-size ordering matches the auth-path ordering, making the two axes indistinguishable on this corpus
C_answer_size_is_a_separate_axis.must_fire_because: if the answer set ordered the sets the same way the auth path does, a single total would be safe to publish and the separation this spike insists on would be decoration
C_answer_size_is_a_separate_axis.name: C_answer_size_is_a_separate_axis
C_answer_size_is_a_separate_axis.null_must_contain: answer sizes free to correlate with the auth path -- nothing in the construction forces the two orderings apart, and on a different corpus they could coincide

C_auth_path_comparison_is_decisive.can_fail_because: fewer than three sets produced proofs, or the largest and smallest auth-path means are within 5% of each other, making the ranking noise
C_auth_path_comparison_is_decisive.must_fire_because: the falsifier here is an ORDERING, so what has to be checked is that the ordering was decidable at all: three sets, real verified proofs, and values far enough apart that the ranking is not noise
C_auth_path_comparison_is_decisive.name: C_auth_path_comparison_is_decisive
C_auth_path_comparison_is_decisive.null_must_contain: auth-path values free to tie or to sit within rounding of each other, in which case no ordering claim could be made in either direction

C_completeness_proofs_verify.can_fail_because: any completeness proof fails verification, or any query fails to cover
C_completeness_proofs_verify.must_fire_because: a completeness proof that its own verifier rejects is a number about nothing, and this is the proof kind whose verifier is the anti-omission check -- W2 drives it to False with C_omit / C_add / C_tamper
C_completeness_proofs_verify.name: C_completeness_proofs_verify
C_completeness_proofs_verify.null_must_contain: W2's verify_completeness, which returns False on an omitted, added or tampered key and is free to reject every proof here

C_queries_are_scale_matched.can_fail_because: mean query length is not close to FRACTION of mean key length for every set
C_queries_are_scale_matched.must_fire_because: a query taken at a fixed BYTE depth sits near the root of a 1,155-byte atom key and near the leaf of a 12-byte triple key, which compares two regimes and calls it a comparison
C_queries_are_scale_matched.name: C_queries_are_scale_matched
C_queries_are_scale_matched.null_must_contain: the key lengths themselves, which differ by 90x across these sets and would produce wildly unmatched query depths under a fixed-byte rule

falsifier.can_fail_because: the completeness auth-path ordering differs from the membership ordering on these three key sets
falsifier.fires_when: the completeness auth-path ordering differs from the membership ordering on these three key sets
falsifier.name: F_branching_rule_is_point_query_only
falsifier.null_must_contain: three key sets free to rank in any of six orders under either measure, so agreement and disagreement are both expressible
falsifier.refutes: S77's "proof size is set by branching, not key length" as a statement about key sets rather than about point queries

verdict.finding: the completeness auth path orders the key sets DIFFERENTLY from membership, so "proof size is set by branching" is a POINT-QUERY claim and S77/S79 must carry that scope
